_meta.indication: REBLOZYL is indicated for the treatment of anemia in adult patients with beta thalassemia who require regular red blood cell (RBC) transfusions.

pivotal_trials.design: Multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial; patients randomized 2:1 to REBLOZYL or placebo, each with best supportive care.
pivotal_trials.population: Adult patients with beta thalassemia who require regular RBC transfusions (6-20 RBC units per 24 weeks); median age 30 years (range 18-66).
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Proportion of patients achieving >=33% reduction from baseline in RBC transfusion burden with a reduction of at least 2 units from Week 13 to Week 24.
pivotal_trials.result: Primary endpoint (Week 13-24): 21.4% (48/224) REBLOZYL vs 4.5% (5/112) placebo; risk difference 17.0 (95% CI 10.4, 23.6); p<0.0001.

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (>=10%): headache (26%), bone pain (20%), arthralgia (19%), fatigue (14%), cough (14%), abdominal pain (14%), diarrhea (12%), dizziness (11%). Serious adverse reactions occurred in 3.6% of patients (cerebrovascular accident and deep vein thrombosis in 1%); thromboembolic events occurred in 8/223 (3.6%) REBLOZYL-treated patients.
target_moa: Erythroid maturation agent; a recombinant fusion protein that binds select endogenous TGF-beta superfamily ligands, thereby diminishing Smad2/3 signaling and improving erythroid maturation/ineffective erythropoiesis.

advisory_committee.vote: The application was not referred to an FDA advisory committee because the safety data did not raise significant safety or efficacy issues that were unexpected in the intended population.

description.text: Added indication for anemia in ESA-naive adult patients with very low- to intermediate-risk MDS who may require regular RBC transfusions

citations.quote: This Prior Approval supplemental biologics license application provides for a new indication for "anemia without previous erythropoiesis stimulating agent use (ESA-naive) in adult patients with very low- to intermediate-risk myelodysplastic syndromes (MDS) who may require regular red blood cell (RBC) transfusions".

summary.text: REBLOZYL (luspatercept-aamt), a new molecular entity, received orphan drug designation (March 11, 2013) and fast track designation (May 5, 2015) for beta-thalassemia, and was reviewed under Priority review. It received traditional (non-accelerated) approval on November 8, 2019 based on the completed primary endpoint of the Phase 3 BELIEVE trial.
